ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a large triangle PRT, with P at the lower left, T at the lower right, and R above; Q is located on side PR, U is located on the base PT, S is located on side RT, and segments such as QS, QU, and US are also drawn in the figure. From the image it can be seen that ray PQ and PR are on the same straight line, and ray PU and PT are on the same straight line, so ∠QPU and the base angle ∠RPT of the large triangle are the same angle. Then reason: It is known that PQ ≅ UQ, so triangle PQU is an isosceles triangle, and the included angle of the equal sides PQ and UQ is ∠PQU = 40°. Therefore the two base angles of triangle PQU are equal, each being (180° - 40°) / 2 = 70°, so ∠QPU = 70°. Because ∠QPU = ∠RPT, ∠RPT = 70°. It is also known that PR ≅ RT, so triangle PRT is an isosceles triangle, and the base angles ∠RPT and ∠RTP are equal, so ∠RTP = 70°. Finally ∠R = 180° - 70° - 70° = 40°.

method.method_draft: From the image, note that Q lies on segment PR and U lies on segment PT, so angle QPU is the same as the large triangle's base angle RPT. From the text, PQ ≅ UQ, so triangle PQU is isosceles with vertex angle ∠PQU = 40. Therefore its two base angles are (180 - 40)/2 = 70, so ∠QPU = 70. Thus ∠RPT = 70. Also from the text, PR ≅ RT, so triangle PRT is isosceles and its base angles at P and T are equal. Hence ∠RTP = 70, and ∠R = 180 - 70 - 70 = 40.
